mainTopic: Making vessels that held a גוי's wine usable: brine, fire, rinsing, cups, and glazed vessels
overview: The גמרא keeps discussing vessels that soaked up a גוי's wine, and how to make them usable again. First it proves that fish brine may be put into old jugs from the start. Then it says firing the jugs in a furnace until the tar softens permits them, but burning splinters inside does not. רב נחמן and רב יהודה forbid putting beer into such jugs and רבא permits it. Next comes a series of vessel types: dung vessels filled with water (and wrongly left in the sun), כלי נתר that can never be fixed, and jugs that need only a rinse, either because the wine was in them only briefly or because they barely absorb. For drinking cups, the הלכה is that a גוי's first or second use forbids them and the third use leaves them permitted. Finally, רב זביד and מרימר argue about glazed vessels of different colors. The גמרא asks why חמץ on פסח should be different, and narrows a question put to מרימר down to smooth white and black vessels. His answer begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next one.

steps.title: Is brine allowed from the start or only after the fact?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether putting ציר and מורייס into a גוי's wine jugs is allowed לכתחילה or only בדיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it allowed from the start, or only after the fact?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a quick question about the rule it just discussed: putting fish brine into a גוי's used wine jugs. Is that allowed from the start, or only if someone already did it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion said brine in these jugs is fine. But 'fine' could mean two things: you may plan to do it (לכתחילה), or you may only use the brine if it already happened (דיעבד). This step opens that question.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start: allowed even as a plan
After the fact: acceptable only once it already happened

phrases.english: Is it from the start, or after the fact?
phrases.notes: This is about putting fish brine into the גוי's used wine jugs, from the lines just before this.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכַתְּחִלָּה אוֹ דִיעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the level of permission for the brine rule discussed just before this section
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether brine may be put into a גוי's wine jugs לכתחילה or only בדיעבד

steps.title: A ברייתא proves brine is allowed from the start
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד בר אושעיא teaches that old jugs bought from a גוי may have ציר and מורייס put in them לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as רב זביד בר אושעיא teaches: someone who buys jugs from a גוי may put wine into new ones, and may put fish brine and fish sauce into old ones, even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a teaching. It openly says 'לכתחילה,' so brine is allowed from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching treats new and old jugs differently. New jugs may even hold wine, while old jugs have soaked up much more wine. Even so, the old jugs may hold brine and fish sauce, and the word לכתחילה settles the question.
steps.whatToRemember: Old jugs a גוי used for wine may have fish brine put into them even from the start.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַב זְבִיד בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rav Zevid bar Oshaya teaches:
One who buys jugs from the gentiles:
new ones, he may put wine into them;

phrases.aramaic: יְשָׁנִים — נוֹתֵן לְתוֹכָן צִיר וּמוּרְיָיס לְכַתְּחִלָּה.
phrases.english: old ones, he may put brine and fish sauce into them, from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַב זְבִיד בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 1's question with a ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Brine may be put in לכתחילה, as the ברייתא says outright

steps.title: What if the jugs were put back into the furnace?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה asks רבי אמי whether a גוי's jugs become permitted if they are put back into a furnace until they glow white.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה נשיאה asked רבי אמי: if someone put the jugs back into the furnace and they turned white-hot, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. Can strong fire clean out the forbidden wine that soaked into the jugs?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the method was brine. Now the question is whether firing the jugs again, the way they were first made, also removes the absorbed wine.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him: one sage asks another

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda Nesia asked Rabbi Ami:
If one returned them to the furnace and they turned white, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from brine to fire as a way to clean the jugs
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether heating the jugs in a furnace makes them permitted

steps.title: If brine works, fire surely works
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers with a קל וחומר: if brine burns out the wine, fire certainly does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: brine burns out the wine. Doesn't fire do so even more?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers that the jugs are permitted. He reasons from the weaker brine to the stronger fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Brine was allowed because its sharpness 'burns away' the absorbed wine. Real fire is stronger than brine, so it surely removes the wine too.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so: a קל וחומר

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: צִיר שׂוֹרֵף, אוּר לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?!
phrases.english: Brine burns it out; fire, all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: צִיר שׂוֹרֵף, אוּר לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Firing the jugs permits them, by a קל וחומר from brine

steps.title: רבי יוחנן also permits jugs refired in a furnace
steps.stepSummary: A statement of רבי יוחנן (some say through רבי אסי) supports רבי אמי: refired jugs whose tar has come off are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי יוחנן said (and some say רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן): a גוי's jugs that were put back into the furnace are permitted once their tar coating has come off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source that agrees with רבי אמי. It also adds a sign for when the jugs count as cleaned: the tar coating comes off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'איתמר נמי' means 'it was also stated.' It shows that another אמורא ruled the same way. רבי יוחנן adds a practical sign: once the tar falls off, the fire has done its job.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated: a supporting statement

phrases.english: It was also stated: Rabbi Yoḥanan said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: קַנְקַנִּים שֶׁל גּוֹיִם שֶׁהֶחְזִירָן לְכִבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ,
phrases.english: Jugs of gentiles that one returned to the furnace,
once their tar has fallen off them, they are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר נָמֵי: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אמי's answer with רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's ruling that firing permits the jugs
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement (or רבי אסי in his name)

steps.title: Softened tar is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the tar does not need to fall off. It is enough if the tar softens.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: don't say the jugs must stay in until the tar falls off. Even if it only softens, the jugs are permitted, even though it did not fall off.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains רבי יוחנן's rule and makes it easier. Softening the tar is already enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, רבי יוחנן's words 'the tar fell off' would demand a lot of heating. רב אשי says the real point is heat strong enough to soften the tar, and that alone permits the jugs.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say: introduces a correction of how one might read a rule

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Do not say: only once it falls off;
rather, even if it merely softened,
even though it did not fall off.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לָא תֵּימָא עַד דְּנָתְרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far רבי יוחנן's tar condition goes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heating until the tar softens is enough to permit the jugs

steps.title: Argument over burning splinters
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא argue whether burning wood splinters inside the jug is enough to permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: About splinters, רב אחא and רבינא argue: one forbids and one permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a weaker way of heating: burning splinters inside the jug. Two sages argue whether this works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A furnace heats the whole jug strongly. Splinters burning inside give only partial heat, so the question is whether that is enough. The גמרא does not say which sage holds which view.

phrases.aramaic: קִינְסָא — פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב אַחָא וְרָבִינָא,
phrases.english: Splinters: Rav Aḥa and Ravina disagree about it,
phrases.notes: He means lighting splinters inside the jug to heat it, instead of using a furnace.

phrases.english: one forbids and one permits,

steps.triggerLanguage: קִינְסָא — פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב אַחָא וְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the furnace to a weaker method of heating
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is an argument whether burning splinters inside permits the jug

steps.title: The הלכה follows the stricter view
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is like the one who forbids splinters.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like the one who forbids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the argument: burning splinters does not permit the jug.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only real furnace heat, as in רבי יוחנן's rule, permits the jugs. The lighter heat of splinters is not relied on.
steps.whatToRemember: Furnace heat that softens the tar permits a גוי's jugs; burning splinters inside does not.

phrases.english: And the law is like the one who forbids.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּמַאן דְּאָסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument in step 7
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Splinters do not permit the jug; the הלכה follows the stricter view

steps.title: May beer be put into such a jug?
steps.stepSummary: The sages ask whether beer may be put into a jug that absorbed a גוי's wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: may one put beer into it?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins: may beer be kept in a jug that still has forbidden wine soaked into it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Brine was allowed because it burns out the wine. Beer does not burn it out, so it is not clear whether putting beer in is allowed. The story in step 11 shows the worry: someone might end up pouring wine into the jug.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them: a question raised in the study hall

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
What is the law about putting beer into it?
phrases.notes: 'It' means a גוי's jug that still has forbidden wine soaked into it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לִיתֵּן לְתוֹכוֹ שֵׁכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about storing beer in the jugs
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether beer may be put into a jug that absorbed forbidden wine

steps.title: Sages argue about beer
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן and רב יהודה forbid putting beer into such a jug, and רבא permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן and רב יהודה forbid it, and רבא permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer to the beer question is an argument: two sages forbid it and one permits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not settled here with one ruling. Instead the גמרא records the different views, and the next step shows how one sage acted in practice.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman and Rav Yehuda forbid,
and Rava permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן וְרַב יְהוּדָה אָסְרִי, וְרָבָא שָׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to step 9 as an argument
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן and רב יהודה forbid beer; רבא permits it

steps.title: רבינא permits beer even after a mistake
steps.stepSummary: רבינא allowed רב חייא בריה דרב יצחק to put beer into such a jug. רב חייא put wine in instead, and רבינא still was not worried, calling it a one-time thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא permitted רב חייא son of רב יצחק to pour beer into it. He went and poured wine into it. Even so, רבינא was not worried about the matter. He said: it is just a one-time happening.
steps.whatsHappening: A story shows רבינא following the lenient view and allowing beer in practice. A mistake that happened along the way did not change his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could worry that allowing beer leads people to put wine in by mistake. רבינא answers that this rare slip is not a reason to forbid beer for everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: רבינא follows רבא and permits beer in such jugs; a one-time mistake does not make the permission forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: רָבִינָא שְׁרָא לֵיהּ לְרַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יִצְחָק
phrases.english: Ravina permitted Rav Ḥiyya, son of Rav Yitzḥak,
to pour beer into it;
he went and poured wine into it.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא חַשׁ לַהּ לְמִילְּתָא,
phrases.english: And even so, he was not concerned about the matter;
phrases.notes: 'He' here is רבינא, who had given the permission.

phrases.english: he said: it is merely a chance occurrence.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא שְׁרָא לֵיהּ לְרַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבינא acting on רבא's lenient view from step 10
steps.raayaObject: The lenient view (רבא) that beer may be put into such jugs
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבינא and רב חייא בריה דרב יצחק

steps.title: רב יצחק בר ביסנא's dung vessels burst in the sun
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר ביסנא filled his dung vessels with water and put them in the sun, and they burst.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר ביסנא had some vessels made of dung. He filled them with water and put them in the sun, and they burst.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about someone trying to clean vessels that had absorbed a גוי's wine. It sets up the comment that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Filling a vessel with water is a known way to draw out absorbed wine. רב יצחק בר ביסנא added an extra step, leaving them in the sun, and the vessels were ruined.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יִצְחָק בַּר בִּיסְנָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Bisna had
certain vessels made of dung,
he filled them with water,
placed them in the sun, and they burst.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יִצְחָק בַּר בִּיסְנָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָנְהוּ מָאנֵי דְּפָקוּסְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the beer-in-the-jug discussion to a new story about cleaning a different kind of vessel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story: dung vessels filled with water and left in the sun burst.

steps.title: רבי אבא: the sun was never part of the method
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא tells him the vessels are now lost to him forever, because the חכמים only said to fill them with water, not to put them in the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to him: You have made them forbidden to yourself forever. Fine, the רבנן said to fill them with water. But did they say to put them in the sun?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא criticizes what רב יצחק בר ביסנא did. He points out that the extra step of the sun was never what the חכמים taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The approved method is only filling the vessel with water. By adding the sun, which the חכמים never said, he broke the vessels, so now he can never use them at all.
steps.whatToRemember: The method for these vessels is filling them with water. Leaving them in the sun was never part of it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to him:
You have forbidden them to yourself with a permanent prohibition.
Granted, the Sages said to fill them with water,
but did they say to place them in the sun?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן מְמַלִּינְהוּ מַיָּא, אַנּוֹחֵי בְּשִׁימְשָׁא מִי אֲמוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the story in step 12 by criticizing the method used.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק בר ביסנא's action of putting the water-filled vessels in the sun
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים only required filling with water. Adding the sun went beyond the rule and destroyed the vessels.

steps.title: Natron vessels can never be made usable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסנא in the name of רבי אמי rules that כלי נתר can never become usable again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסנא said in the name of רבי אמי: Natron vessels have no purification ever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule about one specific kind of vessel. Once it held a גוי's wine, there is no way to fix it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the vessels before, where filling with water helps, this kind of vessel has no cleaning method at all. The word טהרה here means making it usable again, not ritual purity from טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Natron vessels (a kind of mineral vessel)
Here: a way to make it usable again

steps.confusionAlert: טהרה here does not mean ritual purity from טומאה. It means getting rid of the absorbed forbidden wine so the vessel can be used.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסְנָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yusna said that Rabbi Ami said:
Natron vessels have no purification ever.
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'it', the word in round brackets. The corrected wording in square brackets says 'them', to match 'vessels'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסְנָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of vessel types, now giving one that can never be fixed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כלי נתר that held a גוי's wine can never be made usable.

steps.title: What are natron vessels?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly כלי נתר are.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are natron vessels?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the term in רבי אמי's rule means. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To apply the rule, we need to know which vessels count. The question is about the meaning of the term, not about the rule itself.

phrases.english: What are natron vessels?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי כְּלֵי נֶתֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the term used in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of vessel is a כלי נתר?

steps.title: Natron vessels are made from alum diggings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין explains that they are vessels made from material dug out of alum.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין said: Vessels made from the diggings of alum.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר אבין answers the question by naming the material these vessels are made from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know which vessels the rule is talking about. They are made from a material taken out of the ground, and this kind of vessel can never be fixed.
steps.whatToRemember: כלי נתר are vessels made from dug-out alum, and once they hold a גוי's wine they can never be used.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said:
Vessels made from the diggings of alum.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כלי נתר are vessels made from dug-out alum.

steps.title: פרזק seizes jugs, fills them with wine, and returns them
steps.stepSummary: פרזק from the ruler's household seized jugs in פומבדיתא, put wine in them, and returned them, so the owners asked רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: פרזק of the vizier's household seized some jugs from פומבדיתא, put wine in them, and returned them. They came and asked רב יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case that brought a question to רב יהודה. It is setting up his ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The jugs belonged to Jews, but a גוי's wine was put in them. The owners need to know if the jugs can still be used, and how.

phrases.english: Parzak, of the vizier's household,
seized certain jugs from Pumbedita,
put wine in them,
and returned them to them.
They came and asked Rav Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ שַׁיְילוּהּ לְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case about another kind of vessel, brought to רב יהודה for a ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are the jugs that held the גוי's wine usable, and how are they cleaned?

steps.title: רב יהודה: rinse them in water, since the wine was not put in for storage
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that because the wine was put into these jugs only temporarily, not for storage, rinsing them in water is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: It is something that is not brought in for keeping. One rinses them in water, and they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question about the seized jugs. He permits them with just a rinse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key fact is how the wine was put in. Since it was not put there for long-term storage, a simple rinse in water is enough, and no stronger method is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing it in for keeping / long storage

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that how long the wine was kept in a vessel affects how hard it is to make it usable again.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מַכְנִיסוֹ לְקִיּוּם הוּא,
phrases.english: He said: It is an item that one does not bring in for keeping,
phrases.notes: He means the wine wasn't put in these jugs to be stored there for a long time, so not much soaked in.

phrases.english: so one rinses them in water, and they are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מַכְנִיסוֹ לְקִיּוּם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question brought in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The jugs are permitted after rinsing in water, since they are not used for storage.

steps.title: רב עוירא: dark Aramean jugs need only a rinse
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא rules that dark brown Aramean jugs, which barely absorb, are permitted after rinsing in water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא said: These dark brown Aramean jugs, since they do not absorb much, one rinses them in water and they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוירא adds another kind of vessel that only needs a rinse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the reason is different from רב יהודה's. These jugs are permitted because of what they are made of: they barely soak anything in.

phrases.english: Rav Avira said:
These dark brown jugs of the Arameans,
since they do not absorb much,
one rinses them in water and they are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עַוִּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case where rinsing is enough, this time because the material barely absorbs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dark Aramean jugs need only rinsing because they absorb very little.

steps.title: רב פפי: vessels from בי מיכסי need only a rinse
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי rules the same for the vessels from בי מיכסי, since they also barely absorb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: These vessels from בי מיכסי, since they do not absorb much, one rinses them in water and they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי gives one more example using the same reasoning as רב עוירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is the same: vessels that hardly absorb need only a rinse. רב פפי applies it to vessels from another place.

keyTerms.meaning: A place name, where these vessels came from

steps.whatToRemember: Vessels that hardly absorb, like the dark Aramean jugs and the vessels of בי מיכסי, only need rinsing in water. כלי נתר can never be fixed.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said:
These earthenware vessels of Bei Mikhsei,
since they do not absorb much,
one rinses them in water and they are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פַּפִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats רב עוירא's reasoning for a different type of vessel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vessels from בי מיכסי need only rinsing because they absorb very little.

steps.title: Dispute about wine cups
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי forbids cups that a גוי drank wine from, and רב אשי permits them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cups: רב אסי forbade them, and רב אשי permitted them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case: drinking cups that held a גוי's wine. Two אמוראים disagree about whether these cups are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cup holds wine only for a short time, not the way a storage jug does. So it is unclear whether it absorbs enough wine to become forbidden. רב אסי is strict and רב אשי is lenient.

phrases.english: Cups:
Rav Asi forbade them,
and Rav Ashi permitted them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּסֵי — רַב אַסִּי אָסַר, וְרַב אָשֵׁי שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from jugs that barely absorb (Steps 18-20) to a new kind of vessel, the drinking cup.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אסי: cups used by a גוי for wine are forbidden. רב אשי: they are permitted.

steps.title: Where the dispute really is: second use
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees a cup is forbidden if the גוי was the first to drink from it. They argue only about a cup used a second time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a גוי drank from the cups the first time, everyone agrees they are forbidden. They argue when it is the second time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the dispute from Step 21. It shows exactly which case the two אמוראים argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brand-new cup soaks up a lot the first time it is used, so everyone forbids it. A cup that was already used has already soaked up some liquid and has less room to absorb more, so on the second use there is room to argue.

keyTerms.meaning: everyone agrees (literally, all the world does not argue)

phrases.aramaic: אִי שָׁתֵי בְּהוּ גּוֹי פַּעַם רִאשׁוֹן —
phrases.english: If a gentile drank from them the first time,
everyone agrees that it is forbidden;
when they argue, it is about the second time.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דַּאֲסִיר, כִּי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case of the dispute in Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cup used by a גוי first is forbidden by all. The dispute is about the second use.

steps.title: Second version: the dispute is about the third use
steps.stepSummary: Another version says everyone forbids the first and second use, and the argument is only about the third use.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: the first and second time, everyone agrees it is forbidden. They argue about the third time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different tradition about where the line of the dispute falls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the cup must be used even more before anyone permits it. Both the first and second uses are forbidden by all, and only the third use is argued over.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
the first and second time,
everyone agrees that it is forbidden;
when they argue, it is about the third time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of Step 22 that moves the dispute from the second use to the third.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First and second uses are forbidden by all. The dispute is about the third use.

steps.title: The final הלכה for cups
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה: a cup used by a גוי the first or second time is forbidden, and the third time it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: the first and second time, it is forbidden. The third time, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling follows the second version (Step 23) and sides with the lenient view in the third-use case. Once a cup has been used enough, it no longer absorbs enough wine to become forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: Cups: first and second use by a גוי make them forbidden, and the third use leaves them permitted.

phrases.english: And the halacha is:
the first and second time, it is forbidden;
the third time, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute using the framing of Step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A cup a גוי drank wine from for the first or second time is forbidden. From the third time on, it is permitted.

steps.title: רב זביד on glazed vessels by color
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד: white and black glazed vessels are permitted, green ones are forbidden because of the alum, and cracked ones are all forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: Glazed earthenware vessels that are white or black are permitted. Green ones are forbidden, because they contain alum. If they have cracks, all of them are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement about glazed earthenware vessels (קוניא). רב זביד sorts them by color.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The glaze usually blocks absorption, so white and black vessels are permitted. Green glaze contains alum, which absorbs well, so those vessels are forbidden. If there are cracks, wine gets into the clay underneath, so every color becomes forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
These glazed earthenware vessels:
white and black ones are permitted;
green ones are forbidden, because they contain alum.
And if they have cracks in them,
they are all forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד: הַאי מָאנֵי דְקוּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from cups to glazed earthenware vessels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: White and black קוניא are permitted, green קוניא is forbidden, and cracked vessels of any color are forbidden.

steps.title: מרימר permits every color
steps.stepSummary: מרימר taught publicly that glazed vessels of every color, even green, are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר taught: Glazed earthenware, whether black, white, or green, is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר disagrees with רב זביד and is lenient even about the green vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For מרימר, the glaze itself keeps wine from soaking in, so the color makes no difference. This argues with רב זביד's ruling against green vessels.

phrases.english: Mareimar taught:
Glazed earthenware, whether black or white
or green, is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ מָרִימָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב זביד (Step 25) about green vessels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Glazed earthenware of every color is permitted for wine.

steps.title: How is this different from חמץ on פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why מרימר's leniency should be different from חמץ on פסח, and it starts quoting a question asked of him about using glazed vessels on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from חמץ on פסח? For they asked מרימר: These glazed earthenware vessels, may one use them on פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges מרימר's ruling by comparing it to חמץ. It is setting up the next move by quoting a question that was put to מרימר about פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If glazed vessels are permitted for wine because they barely absorb, the same reason should apply to חמץ. The quoted question about פסח is brought to show that מרימר seems to treat the two cases differently. מרימר's answer begins in step 30 and continues on the next amud.
steps.confusionAlert: מרימר's answer about פסח has not been quoted yet. Do not assume the outcome; it begins at the end of the amud (step 30) and continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: How is this different from leavened food on Pesach?
For they asked Mareimar:
These glazed earthenware vessels,
what is the law about using them on Pesach?
phrases.notes: He means vessels that held חמץ during the year. Can they be used on פסח?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מֵחָמֵץ בַּפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges מרימר's lenient ruling in Step 26 by comparing it to the case of חמץ.
steps.kashyaTarget: מרימר's ruling that all glazed vessels are permitted for wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Absorption should work the same way for wine and for חמץ, so a different ruling for פסח would be inconsistent.

steps.title: The question is only about white and black
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that green vessels are clearly forbidden for פסח, so the real question was only about white and black ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not ask about green ones, since they contain alum, absorb, and are forbidden. Ask about white and black ones: what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the quoted question, the גמרא narrows it down. Green vessels are obvious, and the doubt is only about white and black ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Green glaze contains alum and absorbs, so for חמץ it is clearly forbidden. The open question is about white and black vessels, which are the ones that barely absorb.

phrases.english: About green ones, do not ask,
since they contain alum, absorb, and are forbidden.
Where you should ask is
white and black ones: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: יְרוּקֵּי לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question quoted in Step 27 down to white and black vessels.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether white and black glazed vessels that held חמץ may be used on פסח.

steps.title: Cracked vessels are not part of the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets aside cracked glazed vessels, since they surely absorb and are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the vessels have cracks in them, you would not ask about them at all, because they certainly absorb what was in them and are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps narrowing the question asked of מרימר about using glazed vessels on פסח. It removes cracked vessels from the question because their answer is obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 already removed green vessels from the question. Now cracked vessels are removed too: a crack lets food soak into the vessel, so it surely holds absorbed חמץ and is forbidden. This fits רב זביד's rule in step 25 that cracked vessels are all forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Cracks in the glaze of a vessel
You should not ask about it; the answer is obvious
They absorb (taste or food soaks into the vessel)

phrases.english: When they have cracks in them,
phrases.notes: "They" means the white and black glazed vessels from step 28.

phrases.english: do not ask the question,
since they certainly absorb and are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אִית בְּהוּ קַרְטוּפָנֵי, לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 28's narrowing of the question. Step 28 removed green vessels, and this step removes cracked ones.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Sets the limits of the question asked of מרימר by ruling out cracked vessels, whose status is already clear.

steps.title: The real question: smooth vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the true question: what is the law for smooth glazed vessels? Then it begins to bring מרימר's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where you should ask the question is about smooth vessels: what is the law? He said...
steps.whatsHappening: After clearing away green and cracked vessels, the גמרא names the one case that is really in doubt: smooth white or black glazed vessels. The last word, "he said," sets up מרימר's answer, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smooth glaze might keep food from soaking in, so maybe such vessels could be used on פסח. On the other hand, perhaps even smooth glaze absorbs a little. That is the doubt, and it tests how far מרימר's leniency in step 26 really reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Where you should ask the question; this is the real doubt

steps.whyThisMatters: After all the narrowing, the question about פסח is limited to the one case where the vessel's surface itself decides whether it absorbs. מרימר's answer will show whether smooth glaze is trusted for חמץ.

phrases.english: Where you should ask: when they are smooth, what is the law?
He said
phrases.notes: This is מרימר starting his answer. The answer itself continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ — דְּשִׁיעִי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 29 removes cracked vessels, this step states the one remaining case, smooth vessels, and begins to bring the answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether smooth white or black glazed vessels used for חמץ may be used on פסח.
